headline: 3 dead as boundary wall collapses at Mirpur University College
summary: The death toll rose to three after a woman succumbed to her injuries on Tuesday night; a probe committee has been formed to investigate the tragedy.
details: The death toll from the collapse of a boundary wall at Mirpur University College has risen to three. The third victim, 50-year-old Beauty Begum, died while undergoing treatment at the National Institute of Traumatology and Orthopaedic Rehabilitation on Tuesday night.

The other two victims were identified as cleaner Nasima Begum, 44, and rickshaw puller Md Firoz, 41. At least five other people were injured in the incident and are receiving treatment at various hospitals.
Beauty Begum had moved to Dhaka from Joypurhat to escape poverty. She had gone to buy flour from a Trading Corporation of Bangladesh truck sale on the day of the collapse.
The college's governing body chairman, Munshi Bazlul Basit Anju, announced that a seven-member probe committee has been tasked to submit its report within seven working days.
A three-member committee headed by the vice-principal has also been formed to coordinate with the victims' families and provide compensation.

The boundary wall, originally built five feet high in 2002, was raised by another five feet in 2014. An office assistant at the college noted that a large portion of the wall, which lacked pillars or beams, caved in.

headline: Digital shift: Banks can now partner with foreign payment platforms like PayPal
summary: Bangladesh Bank has issued new guidelines allowing banks to tie up with global providers to process outward remittances, potentially opening doors for PayPal and Stripe.
details: The Bangladesh Bank has allowed banks to partner with foreign payment platforms to process outward remittances, aiming to modernize the payment ecosystem and widen digital financial inclusion.

Analysts suggest this move could attract global payment platforms such as PayPal and Stripe into the Bangladesh market, benefiting freelancers, e-commerce businesses, and cross-border service providers.
The central bank's circular introduces Cross-Border Digital Payment Service Providers (CDPSPs) and the concept of Digital Value Accounts (DVAs), which are digital wallets opened in users' names.
These DVAs will operate under a Master DVA maintained by the bank, allowing users to make cross-border online payments up to a specified limit.
The accounts can be used for travel-related foreign exchange transactions, including medical, private, and official travel, as well as payments for IT services, visa fees, and hotel bookings.
The facility may also be extended to top-level officials of eligible entities using Export Retention Quota (ERQ) accounts and Resident Foreign Currency Deposit (RFCD) accounts.
Banks must obtain prior clearance from the central bank before launching these services and must disclose full details of their partnerships and compliance arrangements.
Previously, banks were only permitted to use Online Payment Gateway Service Providers (OPGSPs), which primarily handled small-value inward remittances.
